prose.title: Gride Worked the Phones All Summer and Came Out With Mahomes and St. Brown
prose.dek: Matt Gerardi made {{f.team.0003.trades_s2}} trades between the draft and the lock, flipped a tag and a same-day extension into Amon-Ra St. Brown, and paid {{f.team.0003.faa_13116_price}} for Patrick Mahomes. The preseason simulation still ranks Gride {{f.team.0003.power_rank|ord}}, and there is a lot of season to change that.

paragraphs: April was a roster without a single top-twelve starter. Gerardi had {{f.team.0003.active_roster_opening}} active players and {{f.team.0003.cap_opening}} in salary; Sam Darnold and Cam Skattebo were solid, and the other {{f.team.0003.holes_opening}} spots were holes: Chris Rodriguez at the second running back spot, DJ Moore and Michael Pittman at receiver, David Njoku at tight end, Deebo Samuel and Jalen Coker in the flexes, and Bryce Young in the superflex.

Before the draft he made one move, and it was a big one. Young's rookie deal was running out, and Gerardi extended him in May at {{f.team.0003.contract_16148_salary}} this year and {{f.team.0003.contract_16148_tcv}} in all. The other three expiring rookies, Rodriguez, Kendre Miller and Tyjae Spears, went to the Expired Rookie Auction and to other teams.

t.0003.slot_bridge.title: April: who held each priced slot

paragraphs: Then he got busy. Gerardi tagged Travis Etienne at {{f.team.0003.contract_15253_salary}}, and two days later the tag was a chip: Etienne and 1.07 went to Real Deal Creel for 1.04, where Gride took Jadarian Price. Over draft week he made four more deals, moving up and down the board, and came out with {{f.team.0003.rookie_picks_count}} picks, three of them first-rounders: Price at 1.04, Jordyn Tyson at 1.05, a slot that has produced a usable player half the time, and Antonio Williams at 1.11, plus Chris Bell at 2.03 and Trey Smack at 6.03, who is already his starting kicker.

July brought the second chip. On the same day, Gerardi extended Sam Darnold at {{f.team.0003.contract_13592_salary}} this year and sent him to L.A. Looks with Coker and Emmett Johnson for Amon-Ra St. Brown, Shedeur Sanders and {{f.team.0003.trade_blind_bid_cash}} of blind-bid money. That deal alone took on {{f.team.0003.trade5_salary_in}} of salary and sent {{f.team.0003.trade5_salary_out}} away, and it bought a High-end WR1. On lock day he cut Pittman, {{f.team.0003.cut_14842_salary}} of salary with a {{f.team.0003.cut_14842_penalty}} penalty, to make the room back.

t.0003.moves_s2.title: From the draft to the auction lock

paragraphs: The auction was quarterbacks and nothing else of size. Patrick Mahomes cost {{f.team.0003.faa_13116_price}} and Malik Willis {{f.team.0003.faa_15694_price}} after fourteen bids; every other one of his {{f.team.0003.faa_lots_won}} wins cost the minimum. Mahomes is the Very good and Willis the Good in the What it bought column, and the league table ranks the money {{f.team.0003.faa_off_rank|ord}} of {{f.league.teams}} for what each dollar added.

Mahomes signed a multi-year deal the day he was won and had it restructured the same afternoon, front-loaded to {{f.team.0003.contract_13116_salary_2}} this year with the {{f.team.0003.contract_13116_tcv}} total unchanged, using the room the Pittman cut had opened. Willis got his multi-year deal in September, {{f.team.0003.contract_15694_salary}} this year and {{f.team.0003.contract_15694_tcv}} in all. No waiver claims, one late release of a minimum receiver, and {{f.team.0003.cap_current_room}} of room left.

The lineup it built has {{f.team.0003.studs_today}} top-twelve starters, Mahomes and St. Brown, with Skattebo and Willis solid, and {{f.team.0003.holes_today}} holes: Price at the second running back spot, DJ Moore at receiver, Hunter Henry at tight end, and Deebo Samuel and Kimani Vidal in the flexes. His backs and his tight ends both rank last in the league. Bryce Young, extended in May, is on the bench.

t.0003.moves_s3.title: From the auction to week one

captions.t.0003.faa_value: Ranked by how much each owner's starting offense improved between the auction lock and the close, for every dollar he spent on quarterbacks, backs, receivers and tight ends at the Free Agent Auction. What it bought sorts those buys by grade at their position: Elite, Very good, Good or Depth.

paragraphs: Gerardi has been here since {{f.team.0003.hist_first_season}}, {{f.team.0003.hist_seasons}} completed seasons, and his one title, in {{f.team.0003.hist_title_years}}, came in one of his two division-winning years, {{f.team.0003.hist_div_title_years}}. It is a thin record around a real trophy: {{f.team.0003.hist_playoffs}} playoff trips and a {{f.team.0003.hist_allplay_pct}} career all-play record.

LEGION OF BOOM is a hard room for the team the simulation ranks last. Blake Bombers are {{f.league.power_rank_0010|ord}}, CBP is {{f.league.power_rank_0002|ord}}, and Gride is {{f.team.0003.power_rank|ord}}, with {{f.team.0003.sim_p_playoffs}} playoff odds and {{f.team.0003.sim_p_title}} title odds. Gerardi plays Blake and Whitman five times each.

The next three years, as Gride would put them... 2027.. the rookies arrive, Price and Tyson start, and Gride makes the playoffs... 2028... Mahomes and St. Brown one more time, and Gride announces it in the third person.... 2029..... a second title, and nobody hears about it for a quarter
Week one started well for the team at the bottom: with {{f.league.wk_teams_final}} NFL teams done, Deebo Samuel scored a touchdown and Gride has {{f.team.0003.wk_points_final}} points in the bank.

captions.t.0003.week1: Only games that had finished when this was written. A blank line means he recorded no scoring stat or did not play.
